title: Public Fields & Serialization
description: Expose variables to the Inspector with public and [SerializeField], and understand serialization.

slides.title: Public vs Private 🔓🔒
slides.content:
# Access Modifiers

By default, class members in C# are **private** (not visible outside the class). To expose a variable:

- **public**: accessible from other scripts and shown in the Inspector.
- **private**: hidden from other scripts and hidden in Inspector (unless you use `[SerializeField]`).

```csharp
public int score;      // visible in Inspector, accessible from other scripts
private int secret;    // hidden everywhere
int alsoSecret;        // default is private
```

quizData.question: What is the default access modifier for class members in C#?
quizData.explanation: If you don't specify, class members are private by default.

slides.title: [SerializeField] Attribute 🏷️
slides.content:
# Show Private Fields in Inspector

Sometimes you want to keep a variable private (to prevent other scripts from modifying it) but still tweak it in the Editor. Use `[SerializeField]`:

```csharp
[SerializeField] private float speed = 5f;
```

Now `speed` shows up in the Inspector, but other scripts cannot access it directly. This follows the principle of **encapsulation**.

You can also serialize other types: custom classes (with `[System.Serializable]`), lists, arrays.

quizData.question: What does [SerializeField] do?

options.text: Makes a private field visible in the Inspector
Converts the variable to a string

quizData.explanation: It tells Unity to serialize (save) and display the field in the Inspector.

slides.title: What is Serialization? 💾
slides.content:
# Saving and Loading Data

**Serialization** is the process of converting an object into a format that can be saved and restored. In Unity, serialized fields are automatically saved with the scene or prefab.

- Public fields are serialized by default.
- Private fields with `[SerializeField]` are also serialized.
- Not all types are serializable (e.g., `Dictionary` is not directly serializable).

This means when you change a value in the Inspector, it sticks with the object. When you restart Unity or share the project, those values remain.

slides.title: Serializing a Custom Class
slides.content: You can even create your own serializable data structures.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Hide Public Fields

If you want a variable to be public (for other scripts) but NOT shown in the Inspector, use `[HideInInspector]`:
```csharp
[HideInInspector] public float internalTimer;
```
The field remains accessible from code but stays out of the cluttered Inspector.
